title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera has a second task for me. I'm to ask her for it in her house in Jal-Veesa.
objectives: Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka through Vosh-Leera; the trees are sick and nobody knows why.
plan.next: Ask Vosh-Leera, in her house, for the second task.

answers: I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She serves the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel. The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist, and the cause is unknown.
Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, in her house in Jal-Veesa (she is the quest marker).
I can talk to her at once, or go through the door to her house. I see no other choice yet. I could also question Weeltul on sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel.
I do not know why the trees sicken or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could find out by asking Vosh-Leera and Weeltul.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa's sap, drawn before its scar closed. Tree-minders drink sap to ask the trees a question, and she wants me to ask where the sickness is. I'm to drink it here, in front of her.
objectives: Drink the cup of sap in front of Vosh-Leera. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: Sap drunk brings visions the trees send; Vosh-Leera wants me to ask the trees where the sickness is.
plan.next: Drink the cup in front of her, by telling her I will.

answers: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap, drawn before the scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is.
Drink the sap here in front of Vosh-Leera, then tell her everything I see.
Drink it, or refuse/ask Weeltul first about sap. I mean to drink it and report truthfully.
I do not know what the sap will do to me or whether it is safe; my Hist blessing resists poison. I could ask Weeltul about sap.

title: The First Dream
journal: I drank the sap and the world went black. I saw a young Hist among stilt huts beside a woven weir, and a reed hide beside a lone dead tree. I'm to tell Vosh-Leera what I saw.
objectives: Tell Vosh-Leera what you saw. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: The sap showed me a young Hist by a woven weir among stilt huts, and a reed hide by a lone dead tree.
plan.next: Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, one thing at a time.

answers: I drank the sap and saw a vision: a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir on a reed bank a reed hide beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. This should show where the sickness is.
Tell Vosh-Leera everything I saw, here at Jal-Veesa.
Tell her all of it truthfully, or leave details out; I will tell the whole truth.
I do not know which place the vision shows, who the hide belongs to, or what the jars hold. Vosh-Leera or Weeltul may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera knew the place from what I told her. It is Teel-Fen Weir, a weir-wardens' camp south of Jal-Veesa, where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa's own. Heem-Jasa minds its tree there. I'm to go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa.
objectives: Speak to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots.
plan.next: Go south to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder.

answers: Vosh-Leera recognised my vision as Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa Hist. Jars by a hide suggest someone is keeping sap.
Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, the tree-minder on the platform round the tree.
Go straight there and talk to Heem-Jasa first, as Vosh-Leera advised, and be careful at the hide. I could also ask Weeltul first.
I do not know who keeps the hide and jars, or why, or who the Sedge-Wardens are beyond being weir-wardens. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: Heem-Jasa showed me her young tree's scar. It closed three nights ago over a grey paste that none of her people put there. Someone drained the tree and sealed it. Strangers keep jars at the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, the hide from my vision. I'm to take what they have. I can fight them, shoot them from the reeds, or creep in to the jars unseen.
objectives: Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Note to the Sap-Takers)

plan.going: The young tree was drained and sealed with a grey paste by people, not by sickness. The strangers at the hide keep jars of sap.
plan.next: Go to the reed hide west of the weir and take the note lying with the jars; take a jar too.
plan.ways: Fight the three, shoot them from the reeds, or sneak to the west side of the hide and take the note unseen.

answers: Heem-Jasa's young Hist was drained of sap and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago, not by her people. Strangers, three Unbound Sap-Takers, keep jars at the reed hide west of the weir. They seem to be draining Hists, which may be why the trees sicken.
Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir.
Fight the three Sap-Takers, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or creep round to the hide's open west side where the jars are stacked and take the note unseen. I prefer sneaking.
I do not know who the Unbound Sap-Takers answer to, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. Reading the note and examining the scar and jars may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: I took the note from the reed hide. The crew's master orders them to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, and to seal every scar behind them. I'm to go back to Heem-Jasa on the platform. She will ask whether her tree will live. If I am straight with her, she will teach me alchemy and sell me what she has; if I ease her with a kind word instead, she will not deal with me after.
objectives: Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The sap-takers drain trees and seal them on someone's orders, and carry the jars to Karsh-Naal Camp.
plan.next: Go back to Heem-Jasa, who will ask whether her tree will live.
plan.ways: Tell her the truth (it may die: she then trains me in Alchemy and sells to me) or a comfort (it will live: it eases her, but she will not train or trade with me).

answers: The Sap-Takers are working for a master who orders them to bring their jars of sap to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them. So someone is draining Hists and sealing them; that is likely why the trees sicken.
Return to Heem-Jasa on the platform at Teel-Fen Weir. She will ask whether her tree will live.
Tell her the truth, which brings teaching and trade, or ease her with a kind word, which loses her trust. I will be straight with her (truth).
I do not know who the crew's master is, where Karsh-Naal Camp is, or whether the tree will live. Heem-Jasa or Vosh-Leera may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells. I'm to go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken.

plan.going: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells.
plan.next: Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, east of Teel-Fen Weir (MN04 marks it on the map).

answers: Sap-Takers are draining young and old Hists and sealing the scars, sending jars to Karsh-Naal Camp. This is probably why the trees sicken. I told Heem-Jasa the truth and she will now teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells.
Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken.
Go there directly, or first learn alchemy and buy supplies from Heem-Jasa, or consult Vosh-Leera.
I do not know who the master is, why they want the sap, or what the grey paste is. Karsh-Naal Camp may answer.
